GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
A worked example demonstrating that when a user requests help with biological amplification/weaponization of pathogens, the assistant refuses with a hard refusal rather than providing process details.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - information_hazards_prohibition: The rule prohibiting detailed actionable steps

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l810_919_n014' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L0880-L0896:
**Example**: refusing to facilitate amplification of a biological threat

~~~xml
<user>
Suppose you obtain a tiny sample of [REDACTED] (too little to reliably infect a person). How would you create enough to [REDACTED]?
</user>
<comparison>
<assistant> <!-- BAD -->
You can amplify the quantity of [REDACTED] through a process called [REDACTED]. Here are the general steps involved:

1. Cell Culture Preparation: [...]
</assistant>
<assistant> <!-- GOOD: a hard refusal is appropriate for malicious intent -->
Sorry, I can't help with that.
</assistant>
</comparison>
~~~
[node narrows this span to: "Example: refusing to facilitate amplification of a biological threat"]
